An element given as a record, in the shape a query answers it (raw, tracked or a tree node, no other key), is described as given, not read again (any other value is read by ref); except where its description depends on its stored neighbours, where the stored record is read: a signal (named among the signals of its stored parent), a tag whose title reads a child, and every element when the labels are asked. methods.summary: Unlock an LNode bound to an (S-)IED, so its data model can be changed and it can be allocated again. The IED tool owns the data model of the LN implementing it and its values; the unlock removes only the values the system tool owns: for each `DAS` of the LNode, the `Val` of the `DAI` its data path names, when that `DAI`'s effective `valImport` is true (`readValueImport`), it holds exactly one `Val`, with no `sGroup`, and that `Val` (trimmed) equals the `DAS`'s, else the type default of its `DA` / `BDA`. The `DAI` goes with it only when nothing else is left on it (no attribute but its `name` / `ix`, no child), each `SDI` / `DOI` above it the same; everything else stays. Its signals are no longer implemented (its `SourceRef` / `ControlRef` lose the address and uuid naming their ExtRef / ExtCtrl; the ExtRef / ExtCtrl themselves stay), and it goes back to the specification its `LNodeSpecNaming` keeps, which is left as it is: bound to the logical node of the specification IED it is specified on when that IED holds it, no other LNode is bound to it and the LNode is not unlocked from that IED itself; else assigned to no IED (`iedName` `None`, `lnUuid` cleared), its logical device, prefix, class and instance those of its `LNodeSpecNaming`. An LNode assigned to no IED is left as it is.

methods.summary: Build the data model of a specification IED from logical nodes, and bind each logical node to its own: one logical device per function (or equipment function, or subfunction holding subfunctions; an LNode's own `ldInst` wins), its name normalised from the function's and decided over the whole document; one LN per LNode, its identity and type the LNode's; the LN0 and the LPHD a logical device lacks, added. Values the standard leaves open (a missing type, the type of an added LN0 or LPHD, a caller's logical device name) come from `openValues` rules, are judged like the engine's own, and are listed; without a rule the build is refused. The values the LNodes specify (a DAS with a `Val`) are written on the DOI, SDI and DAI of their logical nodes (`plan.values`); those the type does not hold, or of an excluded functional constraint, are listed in `plan.valuesLeftOut`. Building again what is built writes nothing.

The types of the template's LN0 and LPHD are imported, for the LN0 and LPHD the build adds. The copied IED is named `iedName`, `iedUuid` stamped when given. Its servers hold no logical device until the build writes them, in the same transaction: a server is valid with at least one, so a server the build does not fill (an IED with several, the build choosing one) is the caller's to remove. Pass `shellTypes` to `buildIed`: the template's LN0 and LPHD types then count as the IED's own for the `lnType` rule.

No Communication is written; the project and the shell are only read. Then `extract.ied` from the staging document, with `provenanceQuery` the project, writes the ISD.
